20819.text: The process of aggregation of colloidal particles into an insoluble precipitate by the addition of suitable electrolyte is called
20819.sol: The process of aggregation of colloidal particles into an insoluble precipitate by the addition of an electrolyte is known as coagulation or flocculation. 22775.text: Which of the following waves are used to treatment of muscles ache?

Both Statement I and Statement II are true
38787.sol: For resonance to occur the condition is X L = X C . So, both inductor and capacitor is required. The power factor is given by cos ϕ . 71128.subject: Biology
71128.text: Which of the following is an example of Cytokine barrier?
71128.sol: Innate immunity consists of four types of barriers. Cytokine barriers are one of them. Virus-infected cells secrete proteins called interferons which protect non-infected cells from further viral infection. Therefore, interferons are an example of a cytokine barrier. Answer: Interferon

71168.subject: Biology
71168.text: The process of fertilization of a human egg can be confirmed by the presence of __________.
71168.sol: In human females, the secondary oocyte is arrested in the metaphase II stage of meiosis II before ovulation. The completion of meiosis II occurs only when a sperm enters the secondary oocyte during fertilization. Upon the entry of the sperm, the secondary oocyte completes its second meiotic division, resulting in the formation of a large ovum (ootid) and a small second polar body. Therefore, the presence of the second polar body is a definitive confirmation that the process of fertilization has occurred. Answer: 2^

71252.subject: Biology
71252.text: Wobble hypothesis is useful to explain the __________ property of genetic code.
71252.sol: The Wobble hypothesis was proposed by Francis Crick to explain the degeneracy of the genetic code. According to this hypothesis, the first two bases of a codon form standard Watson-Crick base pairs with the last two bases of the anticodon, while the third base of the codon (the wobble position) can form non-standard base pairs with the first base of the anticodon. This flexibility allows a single tRNA molecule to recognize and bind to more than one codon, which explains why multiple codons can code for the same ami

Definitive nucleus (I). n (B). Synergid (II). 3n (C). Primary Endosperm Nucleus (III). 2n Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
71486.sol: The definitive nucleus, also known as the secondary nucleus, is formed by the fusion of two haploid polar nuclei before fertilization. Thus, its ploidy level is 2n . Synergids are cells present in the egg apparatus of the embryo sac and are formed by mitotic divisions of the functional megaspore. Thus, their ploidy level is n . The Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN) is formed during double fertilization by the fusion of a haploid male gamete ( n ) with the diploid definitive nucleus ( 2n ). Thus, its ploidy level is 3

71909.subject: Chemistry
71909.text: Which one of the following polymers is prepared by addition polymerisation?
71909.sol: Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene) is prepared by the addition polymerisation of tetrafluoroethylene ( CF₂=CF₂ ) under high pressure in the presence of a free radical catalyst. Nylon-6,6 is a condensation polymer formed from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid. Novolac is a condensation polymer formed from phenol and formaldehyde. 71913.subject: Chemistry

71913.sol: Nylon 6,6 is a condensation polymer formed by the reaction of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid under high pressure and at high temperature. 73935.sol: Iodine is an essential trace element required by the thyroid gland to synthesize thyroid hormones, primarily thyroxin (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3). 73939.sol: - Monocyte: A type of white blood cell involved in immune response. - Chondrocyte: Cartilage cells found in connective tissue. - Basophil: A type of white blood cell involved in allergic reactions and inflammation. - Lymphocyte: White blood cells crucial for immune defense.

74551.sol: The impulse-momentum theorem states that the change in momentum of an object equals the impulse applied to it.

protect the plant from herbivorous animals
74883.sol: The correct answer is option C

75169.subject: General Ability
75169.text: Which Ministry has initiated the "Dhara", a special initiative dedicated to Indian Knowledge System (IKS)?
75169.sol: The "Dhara" initiative, which is an ode to the Indian Knowledge System (IKS), was launched by the Ministry of Culture as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav. It comprises a series of events and conferences designed to promote and showcase India's rich heritage, traditions, and knowledge systems across various domains. Answer: The Ministry of Culture

75401.subject: General Ability
75401.text: Which one of the following is not a writ?
75401.sol: The Indian Constitution has authorized the Supreme Court to issue writs in case of enforcement of fundamental rights. These fundamental rights have been granted by Part III under Article 32 of the Indian Constitution. This authority is basically to ensure that the Right to Constitutional Remedies is available to every Indian citizen. There are five types of writs issued which are Mandamus, Certiorari, Quo Warranto, Prohibition and Habeas Corpus.

75489.subject: General Ability
75489.text: A common High Court for two or more states can be established by
options: a law passed by the Parliament
an order of the Supreme Court of India
an order of the President of India
an amendment to the Constitution of India
75489.sol: A common High Court for two or more states or two or more States and a Union territory can be established by a law passed by the Parliament of India. Calcutta high court serves as the high court of Anadaman & Nicobar islands and West Bengal. Similarly, Bombay high court is the high court for Maharashtra, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

79826.subject: Botany
79826.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: During G 0 phase of cell cycle, the cell is metabolically inactive. Statement II: The centrosome undergoes duplication during S phase of the interphase. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statemet II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statemet II is incorrect
79826.sol: Some cells, after the mitotic phase exit from the G1 phase and enter the inactive stage called quiescent stage (G 0 ) of the cell cycle. Cells in this stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism. In the S phase of interphase, the cells duplicate their DNA. In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm.

80187.subject: Botany
80187.text: In Kranz anatomy, the bundle sheath cells have
options: thin walls, many intercellular spaces and no chloroplasts
thick walls, no intercellular spaces and large number of chloroplasts
thin walls, no intercellular spaces and several chloroplasts
thick walls, many intercellular space and few chloroplasts
80187.sol: C ₄ plants have a characteristic leaf anatomy, called 'Kranz' anatomy. Kranz means 'wreath' (ring) and is a reflection of the arrangement of cells. The large sized bundle sheath cells may form several layers around the vascular bundles. These cells are characterised by having a large number of agranal chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange and no intercellular spaces.

80264.subject: Botany
80264.text: The pineapple which under natural condition is difficult to blossom has been made to produce fruits throughout the year by application of:
80264.sol: NAA (alpha Naphthalene acetic acid) and 2,4 Dichlorophenoxy acetic acid are synthetic auxins. Normally, auxins inhibit flowering. In litchi and pineapple, it promotes flowering. Related Theory Antiauxins are a group of chemicals that can prevent auxin-action in plants. Transcinnamic acid, ascorbic acid, 7-phenyl butyric acid are some of these antiauxins. Probably, an antiauxin competes with an auxin for the same site of reaction and thus inhibits auxin-action.

80556.subject: Botany
80556.sol: The transfer of pollen from anther to stigma is called pollination. Autogamy also called self-pollination involves the transfer of pollen grains of one flower to the stigma of same flower. Self-pollination occurs only in bisexual or hermaphrodite flowers. Geitonogamy involves the transfer of pollen grains from a male flower to stigma of female flower of same plant Thus, geitonogamy operates only in monoecious plants, ie, the plants having male and female flowers on different places. 80720.subject: Chemistry
80720.text: Which of the following is more basic than aniline?
80720.sol: Benzyl amine is more basic than aniline because the benzyl group is an electron-donating group on account of the + I effect. So, it is capable of increasing the electron density of N of the - NH ₂ group. Thus, because of the higher electron density, the rate of donation of a free pair of electrons is increased, i.e., the basic character is higher. Phenyl and nitro groups are electron attractive groups, so they are able to decrease the electron density of N of - NH ₂ group. Hence, they are less basic than aniline. A

84134.subject: Zoology
84134.text: Which one of the following plasma proteins is involved in the coagulation of blood?
84134.sol: Fibrinogen (factor 1) is a soluble plasma glycoprotein, synthesised by the liver. It is converted by thrombin into fibrin during blood coagulation. Fibrin is then cross-linked by factor XIII to form a clot.

84381.subject: Zoology
84381.text: One of the important consequences of geographical isolation is:
options: no change in the isolated fauna.
84381.sol: Speciation is the evolutionary process for the formation of new species. The species diversity occurs when gene flow within the common pool is interrupted by an isolating mechanism. Related Theory The isolation can occur through geographical separation of population known as allopatric speciation. When a few individuals of a species within the same geographical area suddenly become reproductively isolated and form new species, it is known as sympatric speciation.

115812.text: Why can nitrogen exhibit oxidation states from +1 to +4 but not +5 with halogens?
115812.sol: The paragraph states that nitrogen cannot form compounds in the +5 oxidation state with halogens because it lacks d-orbitals to accommodate electrons from other elements to form bonds.

116002.subject: Chemistry
116002.text: Which halogen forms the smallest F-F bond dissociation enthalpy?
116002.sol: Fluorine forms the smallest F-F bond dissociation enthalpy.

116806.subject: Chemistry
116806.text: Which element is closely related to the lanthanoids and is often included in discussions about them?
116806.sol: Lanthanum closely resembles the lanthanoids and is usually included in discussions about them.

117022.subject: Chemistry

options: They have strong metallic bonding due to the presence of partially filled d-orbitals.
They have a high number of valence electrons.
They have a high atomic radius.
117022.sol: Correct Option is : (A) They have strong metallic bonding due to the presence of partially filled d-orbitals.

117075.subject: Chemistry
117075.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Despite both having a d⁴ electronic configuration, Cr ²⁺ is strongly oxidizing while Mn ³⁺ is strongly reducing in aqueous solution. Reason (R): Cr ²⁺ readily oxidizes to Cr ³⁺ to achieve a stable half-filled t_ 2g ³ configuration, while Mn ³⁺ readily reduces to Mn ²⁺ to achieve a stable half-fille
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true
117075.sol: Assertion (A) is false because Cr ²⁺ is a strong reducing agent (it undergoes oxidation), while Mn ³⁺ is a strong oxidizing agent (it undergoes reduction). Reason (R) is true. Both Cr ²⁺ and Mn ³⁺ have a d⁴ configuration. Cr ²⁺ acts as a reducing agent because its oxidation leads to Cr ³⁺ , which has a stable half-filled t_ 2g ³ configuration in aqueous medium. 117251.subject: Chemistry
117251.text: According to Werner, which geometrical shapes are more common in coordination compounds of transition metals?
117251.sol: Werner postulated that octahedral and square planar geometrical shapes are more common in coordination compounds of transition metals.

117332.subject: Chemistry
117332.text: What is the primary cause of ionization isomerism in coordination compounds?
options: Interchange of ligands between cations and anions
117332.sol: Ionization isomerism occurs due to the interchange of ligands between cationic and anionic entities of different metal ions in a complex.

117620.subject: Chemistry
117620.text: Which of the following options correctly explains the difference between heteroleptic and homoleptic complexes with examples?
options: Heteroleptic complexes contain only one type of ligand, while homoleptic complexes contain a variety of differ
Heteroleptic complexes contain a mixture of different metal ions, while homoleptic complexes contain only one
Heteroleptic complexes contain different types of ligands bonded to the central metal ion, while homoleptic co
Heteroleptic complexes have a coordination number of 4, while homoleptic complexes have a coordination number
117620.sol: Correct Option is : (C) Heteroleptic complexes contain different types of ligands bonded to the central metal ion, while homoleptic complexes have only one type of ligand bonded to the metal ion. An example of a heteroleptic complex is [Co(NH 3 ) 4 Cl 2 ]Cl, while [Ni(CO) 4 ] is a homoleptic complex.

117863.subject: Chemistry
117863.text: Assertion : The [ Ni ( en )₃ ] Cl ₂ (en = ethylene diamine) has lower stability than [ Ni ( NH ₃ )₆ ] Cl ₂ . Reason : In [ Ni ( en )₃ ] Cl ₂ the geometry of Ni is trigonal bipyramidal.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
117863.sol: [ Ni ( en )₃ ] Cl ₂ is a chelating compound and chelated complexes are more stable than similar complexes with unidentate ligands as dissociation of the complex involves breaking of two bonds rather than one. In [ Ni ( en )₃ ] Cl ₂, Ni with d^8 configuration shows octahedral geometry. Six electrons will occupy the t_ 2 g orbitals and two electrons will occupy the e_g orbitals.

118436.subject: Chemistry
118436.text: Which functional group is present in quinones?
118436.sol: Quinones contain a ketone functional group.

118552.subject: Chemistry
118552.text: What type of compounds are formed when alcohols and phenols react with carboxylic acids, acid chlorides, and acid anhydrides?
118552.sol: Alcohols and phenols react with carboxylic acids, acid chlorides, and acid anhydrides to form esters.

118580.subject: Chemistry
118580.text: Which functional group is responsible for the unique properties of phenols?
118580.sol: The hydroxyl group in phenols is responsible for their distinctive properties, such as hydrogen bonding and solubility.

118977.subject: Chemistry
118977.text: What is the name of the intermediate compound formed when aldehydes react with monohydric alcohol in the presence of dry hydrogen chloride?
118977.sol: The intermediate compound formed when aldehydes react with monohydric alcohol in the presence of dry hydrogen chloride is known as hemiacetal.

119124.subject: Chemistry

119124.sol: (a) Benzoin condensation : Heating ethanolic solution with strong alkali like KCN or NaCN, benzoin is obtained. (b) Formation of phenolphthalein phenol is treated with phthalic anhydride in the presence of conc. H ₂ SO ₄ , it gives phenolphthalein, an indicator. (c) Fries rearrangement Phenyl benzoate heated with anhydrous AlCI ₃ in the presence of inert solvent gives ortho-and Para-hydroxybenzophen one. In this rearrangement, there is only a benzoyl group migration from the phenolic oxygen to an ortho-and para-pos

119310.subject: Chemistry
119310.text: The major product formed in the following conversion is
119310.sol: Major product formed will be a conjugated alkene.

119368.subject: Chemistry
119368.text: Number of stereoisomers formed in the given reaction is
119368.sol: As there is one chiral carbon in the product formed, total number of stereoisomers =2 .

119426.subject: Chemistry
119426.text: What is the role of mineral acid in the preparation of carboxylic acids from Grignard reagents and carbon dioxide?
options: It serves as a reducing agent.
It initiates the reaction with carbon dioxide.
119426.sol: Mineral acid is used to neutralize the Grignard reagent, allowing the formation of carboxylic acids from the salts produced by the reaction with carbon dioxide.

120039.subject: Chemistry
120039.text: What role does cellulose play in the formation of semi-synthetic polymers?
options: Cellulose is the monomer in semi-synthetic polymers.
Cellulose is a catalyst used in the synthesis of semi-synthetic polymers.
Cellulose serves as the source material for semi-synthetic polymers.
Cellulose is a byproduct in the production of semi-synthetic polymers.
120039.sol: Cellulose serves as the source material for the production of semi-synthetic polymers like rayon.

120140.subject: Chemistry
120140.text: Can nucleic acids, proteins and starch be considered as step growth polymers?
options: Yes, for nucleic acids and proteins, but not starch
No, all three cannot be considered as step growth polymers
Yes, for starch, but not nucleic acids and proteins
Yes, all three are step growth polymers i.e. condensation polymers which are formed by the loss of simple mole
120140.sol: Correct Option is : (D) Yes, all three are step growth polymers i.e. condensation polymers which are formed by the loss of simple molecule like water leading to the formation of high molecular mass polymers.

120171.subject: Chemistry
120171.text: Assertion : Ebonite is highly vulcanised rubber. Reason : Perlon is used in the manufacture of fibres.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
120171.sol: Ebonite is a very hard rubber contains 30-40 % sulphur.

120279.subject: Chemistry
120279.text: How does the sweetness of saccharin compare to cane sugar?
options: Saccharin is 5 times as sweet as cane sugar
Saccharin is 10 times as sweet as cane sugar
Saccharin is 100 times as sweet as cane sugar
Saccharin is 550 times as sweet as cane sugar
120279.sol: Saccharin is about 550 times as sweet as cane sugar.

120370.subject: Chemistry
120370.text: What type of bond between an enzyme and an inhibitor leads to permanent enzyme blockage?
120370.sol: If the bond formed between an enzyme and an inhibitor is a strong covalent bond and cannot be broken easily, the enzyme is blocked permanently.

120737.subject: Chemistry
120737.text: What remains intact in a protein during denaturation?
120737.sol: During denaturation, secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed, but the primary structure remains intact.

121366.subject: Botany
121366.text: What is the main component of cell wall in plants?
121366.sol: Kingdom Plantae includes all eukaryotic chlorophyll-containing organisms commonly called plants. A few members are partially heterotrophic such as the insectivorous plants or parasites. Bladderwort and Venus fly trap are examples of insectivorous plants and Cuscuta is a parasite. The plant cells have an eukaryotic structure with prominent chloroplasts and cell wall mainly made of cellulose.

121695.subject: Botany
121695.text: What is a characteristic of marine algae known as kelps?
options: They are found only in freshwater.
121695.sol: Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic (both freshwater and marine) organisms. They occur in a variety of other habitats: moist stones, soils and wood. Some of them also occur in association with fungi (lichen) and animals (e.g., on sloth bear). The form and size of algae is highly variable, ranging from colonial forms like Volvox and the filamentous forms like Ulothrix and Spirogyra (Figure 3.1). A few of the marine forms such as kelps, form massive plant bodies. The algae

122881.subject: Botany
122881.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The stamens in a flower only remain free. Reason: There may be variation in the length of filaments within a flower, as in Calotropis
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
122881.sol: The stamens in a flower may either remain free or may be united in varying degrees. There may be a variation in the length of filaments within a flower, as in Salvia and mustard.

122942.subject: Botany
122942.text: When a flower can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane passing through the centre is known as ___.
122942.sol: When a flower can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane passing through the centre is known as Actinomorphic.

123128.subject: Botany
123128.sol: In tetradynamous condition there is 4+2 arrangement of stamens i.e., out of six stamens, 4 are long and 2 are short. It is a characterstic feature of members of family Brassicaceae.

123430.subject: Botany
123430.text: Read the following description of a plant tissue: "It consists of dead cells that are spherical, oval or cylindrical in shape, possessing highly thickened walls and very narrow cavities. They are commonly found in the fruit walls of nuts and the pulp of fruits like pear and sapota." Identify the specific tissue described above.
123430.sol: The description given exactly matches sclereids, which are a type of sclerenchyma tissue. According to NCERT, sclereids are spherical, oval or cylindrical, highly thickened dead cells with very narrow cavities (lumen). They are commonly found in the fruit walls of nuts; pulp of fruits like guava, pear and sapota; seed coats of legumes and leaves of tea. Sclerenchyma fibres are thick-walled, elongated and pointed cells. Vessels are cylindrical tube-like structures made of many cells (vessel members) with lignified w

124039.subject: Botany
124039.text: Which type of plastid gives the part of the plant a yellow, orange or red colour?
124039.sol: The chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments which are responsible for trapping light energy essential for photosynthesis . In the chromoplasts fat soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene, xanthophylls and others are present. This gives the part of the plant a yellow, orange or red colour .

124322.subject: Botany
124322.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Ribosomes are known as ribonucleoprotein particles. Reason (R): They are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and about 80 different proteins, and are not surrounded by any membrane. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
124322.sol: Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in all cells. They are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and about 80 different proteins. Because of this biochemical composition (RNA and proteins), they are referred to as ribonucleoprotein particles. Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) correctly explains (A) by providing the exact composition that justifies the term 'ribonucleoprotein'. Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

124508.subject: Botany
124508.text: What does 'r' represent in the exponential growth equation W₁=W₀ e^ r t
124508.sol: If we plot the parameter of growth against time, we get a typical sigmoid or S-curve. The exponential growth can be expressed as W₁=W₀ e^ r t W1 = final size (weight, height, number etc.) W0 = initial size at the beginning of the period r = growth rate t = time of growth e = base of natural logarithms

124852.subject: Botany
124852.text: The dormancy of seed is regulated by
124852.sol: Dormancy is the condition of a seed when it fails to germinate even when the environmental conditions usually considered necessary for germination are available. It is regulated by ABA (Absicsic acid)

124938.subject: Botany
124938.text: What is the breakdown of glucose to pyruvic acid called?
124938.sol: During the process of respiration, oxygen is utilized, and carbon dioxide, water and energy are released as products. The combustion reaction requires oxygen. But some cells live where oxygen may or may not be available. Can you think of such situations (and organisms) where O2 is not available? There are sufficient reasons to believe that the first cells on this planet lived in an atmosphere that lacked oxygen. Even among present-day living organisms, we know of several that are adapted to anaerobic conditions. So

125561.subject: Botany
125561.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. External factors affecting photosynthesis rate include mesophyll cells 2. Blackman's limiting factor comes into play when several factors affect any process 3. At any point the rate will be determined by the factor available at sub-optimal levels. 4. Including the plants in shade or in dense forests, light is rarely a limiting factor in nature.
125561.sol: When several factors affect any [bio] chemical process, Blackman’s (1905) Law of Limiting Factors comes into effect. This states the following: If a chemical process is affected by more than one factor, then its rate will be determined by the factor which is nearest to its minimal value: it is the factor which directly affects the process if its quantity is changed.

125771.subject: Botany
125771.text: What do the androecium and the gynoecium represent in a flower?
125771.sol: Much before the actual flower is seen on a plant, the decision that the plant is going to flower has taken place. Several hormonal and structural changes are initiated which lead to the differentiation and further development of the floral primordium. Inflorescences are formed which bear the floral buds and then the flowers. In the flower the male and female reproductive structures, the androecium and the gynoecium differentiate and develop. You would recollect that the androecium consists of a whorl of stamens rep

125853.subject: Botany
125853.text: Where is the embryo sac located within the ovule?
125853.sol: Recall the definition and types of placentation that you studied in Arising from the placenta are the megasporangia, commonly called ovules. The number of ovules in an ovary may be one (wheat, paddy, mango) to many (papaya, water melon, orchids). The Megasporangium (Ovule). Let us familiarise ourselves with the structure of a typical angiosperm ovule The ovule is a small structure attached to the placenta by means of a stalk called funicle. The body of the ovule fuses with funicle in the region called hilum. Thus,

126142.subject: Botany
126142.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The general metabolic activity of the embryo fastens as it matures Reason: All the seeds germinate after attaining maturity
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
126142.sol: As the seed matures, the general metabolic activity of the embryo slows down. The embryo may enter a state of inactivity called dormancy, or if favourable conditions are available, they germinate

126525.subject: Botany
126525.text: What is the role of zinc in the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase?
options: To form coordination bonds with the substrate.
To be a part of the active site.
To be an essential chemical component.
126525.sol: A number of enzymes require metal ions for their activity which form coordination bonds with side chains at the active site and at the same time form one or more coordination bonds with the substrate, e.g., zinc is a cofactor for the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase. Catalytic activity is lost when the co-factor is removed from the enzyme which testifies that they play a crucial role in the catalytic activity of the enzyme.

126764.subject: Botany
126764.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Chitin, found in the exoskeletons of arthropods, is a complex polysaccharide. Reason (R): Chitin is a heteropolymer made up of chemically modified sugars such as N-acetyl glucosamine. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
126764.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because chitin is indeed a complex polysaccharide found in the exoskeletons of arthropods. Reason (R) is incorrect. Although chitin is made up of chemically modified sugars (N-acetyl glucosamine), NCERT specifies that these complex polysaccharides are mostly homopolymers, not heteropolymers. A homopolymer consists of only one type of monomer repeating throughout the chain. Thus, (A) is correct but (R) is not correct. Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

127813.subject: Botany
127813.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses is the biomass available for consumption to heterotrophs. Statement II: Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by decomposers. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
127813.sol: Statement I is correct. Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) minus respiration losses (R) gives Net Primary Productivity (NPP). According to NCERT, NPP is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers). Statement II is incorrect. Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers, not decomposers. Students often confuse the roles of consumers and decomposers in secondary productivity. Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is in

128061.subject: Zoology
128061.text: Frog's Sensory Features Function A. Nostrils 1. Protects eyes underwater B. Eyes 2. Receives sound signals C. Nictitating membrane 3. Bulged and sensitive to light D. Tympanum 4. Above the mouth
128061.sol: The nostrils are above the mouth, the eyes are bulged, the nictitating membrane protects the eyes underwater, and the tympanum receives sound signals.

128344.subject: Zoology
128344.text: What are the three layers of the adrenal cortex called?
options: Zona reticularis, zona fasciculata, zona medulla
Zona reticularis, zona fasciculata, zona glomerulosa
Zona medulla, zona fasciculata, zona glomerulosa
Zona glomerulosa, zona fasciculata, zona reticularis
128344.sol: The adrenal cortex can be divided into three layers, called zona reticularis (inner layer), zona fasciculata (middle layer) and zona glomerulosa (outer layer). The adrenal cortex secretes many hormones, commonly called as corticoids. The corticoids, which are involved in carbohydrate metabolism are called glucocorticoids. In our body, cortisol is the main glucocorticoid. Corticoids, which regulate the balance of water and electrolytes in our body are called mineralocorticoids. Aldosterone is the main mineralocortic

128441.subject: Zoology
128441.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The pars distalis of pituitary, commonly called anterior pituitary, produces melanocyte stimulating hormone Reason: The pars intermedia produces, growth hormone, prolactin, thyroid stimulating hormone, adrenocorticotrophic hormone, leuteinizing hormone and follicle stimulating hormone
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
128441.sol: The pars intermedia of pituitary, commonly called anterior pituitary, produces melanocyte stimulating hormone. The pars distalis produces, growth hormone, prolactin, thyroid stimulating hormone, adrenocorticotrophic hormone, leuteinizing hormone and follicle stimulating hormone

128600.subject: Zoology
128600.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Neurohypophysis does not synthesise any hormones of its own. Reason (R): Oxytocin and vasopressin are synthesised by the hypothalamus and are transported axonally to the neurohypophysis. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
128600.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because the neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) only stores and releases hormones; it does not synthesise any hormones of its own. Reason (R) is also correct and provides the exact explanation for the assertion. The hormones oxytocin and vasopressin, which are released by the neurohypophysis, are actually synthesised by the hypothalamus and are transported axonally to the neurohypophysis for storage and subsequent release. Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explan

128684.subject: Zoology
128684.sol: Gonadotropins or gonadotropic hormones are as follows. (a) Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) : It stimulates growth of ovarian follicles and their secretion of oestrogen in the female and spermatogenesis in the male. (b) Interstitial Cell Stimulating Hormone (ICSH) : It activates the Leydig's cells of the testis to secrete androgens. In female it stimulates the corpus luteum of the ovary to secrete progesterone. In female ICSH is termed as LH (Luteinizing Hormone).

128727.subject: Zoology
128727.sol: The Brunner's glands are located in duodenum only. They secrete a little enzyme and mucus. The mucus protects the duodenal wall from getting digested. The Brunner's glands open into the crypts of Lieberkuhn.

128840.subject: Zoology
128840.text: What type of circulatory system is present in arthropods and molluscs?
128840.sol: The circulatory patterns are of two types – open or closed. Open circulatory system is present in arthropods and molluscs in which blood pumped by the heart passes through large vessels into open spaces or body cavities called sinuses. Annelids and chordates have a closed circulatory system in which the blood pumped by the heart is always circulated through a closed network of blood vessels. This pattern is considered to be more advantageous as the flow of fluid can be more precisely regulated.

129146.subject: Zoology
129146.text: If due to some injury the chordae tendinae of the tricuspid valve of the human heart is partially non-functional, what will be the immediate effect?
options: The flow of blood into the aorta will be slowed down
The blood will tend to flow back into the left atrium
The flow of blood into the pulmonary artery will be reduced
129146.sol: If cordae tendinae of the tricuspid valve become partially non-functional due to injury then flow of blood into the pulmonary artery will be reduced.

129147.subject: Zoology
129147.sol: Erythroblastosis is a haemolytic disease of new borns. It occurs when father is Rh-positive and mother Rh-nagetive.

129993.subject: Zoology
129993.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. Larynx helps in sound production 2. Nasal chamber opens into trachea 3. The nasal chamber opens into the pharynx, a portion of which is the common passage for food and air. 4. The larynx opens through the larynx region into the trachea 5. The branching network of bronchi, bronchioles and alveoli comprise the heart
129993.sol: Larynx is a cartilaginous box which helps in sound production and hence called the sound box.

130003.subject: Zoology
130003.text: Respiration Type Characteristics A. Aerobic Respiration 1. Occurs in the cytoplasm B. Anaerobic Respiration 2. Occurs in mitochondria C. External Respiration 3. Exchange of gases in lungs D. Internal Respiration 4. Occurs at the cellular level
130003.sol: Aerobic respiration occurs in mitochondria. Anaerobic respiration occurs in the cytoplasm. External respiration refers to gas exchange in the lungs. Internal respiration occurs at the cellular level.

130482.subject: Zoology

130482.sol: The human skull has two occipital condyles, making its articulation dicondylic (A matches with III). In human beings, as in almost all mammals, the number of cervical vertebrae is seven (B matches with II). Each rib has two articulation surfaces on its dorsal end, hence it is called bicephalic (C matches with IV). The joint between adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column is a cartilaginous joint, which permits limited movement (D matches with I). Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I. 130753.subject: Zoology
130753.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the procedure of ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer) used as an assisted reproductive technology?
options: Transfer of embryos with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus.
Transfer of a zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube.
Transfer of embryos with more than 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube.
Transfer of an unfertilized ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube.
130753.sol: ZIFT stands for Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer. According to NCERT, in this procedure, the zygote or early embryos with up to 8 blastomeres are transferred into the fallopian tube to complete their further development. Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus, which is called Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT). Transfer of an unfertilized ovum into the fallopian tube is known as Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer (GIFT). Answer: Transfer of a zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres into

130765.subject: Zoology
130765.text: In the Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) procedure known as ZIFT, which of the following is transferred, and to which specific site in the female reproductive tract?
options: A zygote or an early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube
An embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube
A zygote or an early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres into the uterus
An unfertilised ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube
130765.sol: ZIFT stands for Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer. According to NCERT, in this procedure, the zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) is transferred into the fallopian tube to complete its further development. Transferring an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus is called Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT). Transferring an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female is called Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer (GIFT). 131501.subject: Zoology
131501.text: What is the process of copying genetic information from one strand of DNA into RNA called?
131501.sol: The process of copying genetic information from one strand of the DNA into RNA is termed as transcription . Here also, the principle of complementarity governs the process of transcription, except the adenosine complements now form base pairs with uracil instead of thymine. However, unlike in the process of replication, which once set in, the total DNA of an organism gets duplicated, in transcription only a segment of DNA and only one of the strands is copied into RNA. 132482.subject: Zoology
132482.text: In sickle cell anaemia, the defect is caused by the substitution of a specific amino acid at the sixth position of the beta globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule. Which of the following represents the correct substitution?
132482.sol: Sickle cell anaemia is a genetic disorder caused by a point mutation in the beta globin gene. The defect is caused by the substitution of Glutamic acid (Glu) by Valine (Val) at the sixth position of the beta globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule. This substitution occurs due to a single base change at the sixth codon of the beta globin gene from GAG (which codes for Glutamic acid) to GUG (which codes for Valine). 132685.subject: Zoology
132685.text: Which of the following is an example of homologous structures?
options: Wings of a butterfly and a bird
Eyes of an octopus and a mammal
Forelimbs of whales, bats, and humans
132685.sol: Divergent evolution refers to similar anatomical structures in different species that evolve to perform different functions due to adaptations.Such similarities can be interpreted to understand whether common ancestors were shared or not. For example whales, bats, Cheetah and human (all mammals) share similarities in the pattern of bones of forelimbs. Though these forelimbs perform different functions in thes animals, they have similar anatomical structure – all of them have humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarp

132943.subject: Zoology
132943.text: The hearts and brains of different vertebrates exhibit a similar basic structural plan despite varying degrees of complexity. What type of organs do they represent, and which evolutionary phenomenon do they indicate?
132943.sol: According to NCERT, vertebrate hearts and brains share the same fundamental structural plan and embryonic origin but have evolved to exhibit varying degrees of complexity. Such organs are classified as homologous organs. Homologous structures arise due to divergent evolution, where the same basic structure develops along different directions as adaptations to different needs. Analogous organs, on the other hand, arise due to convergent evolution and have different anatomical origins but similar functions. Answer: H

133010.text: The ________ theory attempts to explain to us the origin of the universe.
133010.sol: The Big Bang theory attempts to explain to us the origin of the universe. It talks of a singular huge explosion unimaginable in physical terms. The universe expanded and hence, the temperature came down.

133912.sol: Blue mold (Penicillium) is involved in Penicillin production. Rhizopus is known as bread mold. Acetobacter is used in vinegar production. Saccharomyces is involved in alcohol production.

133970.subject: Zoology
133970.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Microbes) List-II (Products / Actions) (A) Aspergillus niger (I) Immunosuppressive agent (B) Trichoderma polysporum (II) Clot buster (C) Monascus purpureus (III) Blood-cholesterol lowering agent (D) Streptococcus (IV) Citric acid Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
133970.sol: Aspergillus niger is a fungus used for the production of citric acid. Trichoderma polysporum is a fungus that produces Cyclosporin A, which is used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients. Monascus purpureus is a yeast that produces statins, which act as blood-cholesterol lowering agents. Streptococcus is a bacterium that produces streptokinase, which is modified by genetic engineering and used as a 'clot buster'. Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(II). Answer: (A)

134862.subject: Zoology
134862.text: In recombinant DNA technology, various methods are employed to introduce alien DNA into host cells. Which of the following is a direct (vectorless) method of gene transfer?
134862.sol: Agrobacterium tumefaciens, retroviruses, and bacteriophages act as biological vectors to carry and deliver foreign DNA into specific host cells. Micro-injection is a direct (vectorless) method of gene transfer in which recombinant DNA is directly injected into the nucleus of an animal cell using a micro-pipette, without the involvement of any biological vector. Answer: Micro-injection

134946.subject: Zoology
134946.text: Which of the following is a correct sequence of steps in a PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)?
134946.sol: PCR stands for Polymerase Chain Reaction. In this reaction, multiple copies of the gene (or DNA) of interest is synthesised in vitro using two sets of primers (small chemically synthesised oligonucleotides that are complementary to the regions of DNA) and the enzyme DNA polymerase. Each cycle of Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) has three steps: (i) Denaturation; (ii) Primer annealing; and (iii) Extension of primers. 135152.subject: Zoology
135152.text: Why do host-specific parasites tend to co-evolve with their hosts?
options: To migrate to different host species
To evade detection by the host
To develop mechanisms to counteract the host's defense mechanisms
To adapt to different environmental conditions
135152.sol: Many parasites have evolved to be host-specific (they can parasitise only a single species of host) in such a way that both host and the parasite tend to co-evolve; that is, if the host evolves special mechanisms for rejecting or resisting the parasite, the parasite has to evolve mechanisms to counteract and neutralize them, in order to be successful with the same host species . 6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fbb.sol: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is a peptide hormone secreted by the parathyroid glands. Its secretion is regulated by the circulating levels of calcium ions in the blood. 95291.sol: Meristem are actively dividing cells present at root apex and shoot apex. Parenchyma are living photosynthetic tissue which also carries out storage of food. Collenchyma are living mechanical tissue. Sclerenchyma consists of elongated cells called as fibers and small round cells called as sclereids. Epidermal cells are modified to form stomata for transpiration.

95821.subject: Botany
95821.text: Blue green algae are__________ and members of Kingdom ___________
95821.sol: Cyanobacteria also are known as Blue-Green algae are the photosynthetic organisms with chlorophyll 'a' similar to higher plants. Unlike other bacteria, they carry out oxygenic photosynthesis as they are capable of utilizing water as a source of hydrogen in photosynthesis. They are placed in kingdom monera due to their prokaryotic nature.

96654.sol: An ecosystem can be of several types like terrestrial or aquatic, larger or smaller etc. In small pond also an ecosystem can be maintained. 96864.subject: Botany
96864.text: What is the correct difference between the following diagrams? (I) (II)
options: Absence of sub-stomatal chamber in both types of the leaves in (I).
96864.sol: I is the cross section of dicot leaf while II is the cross section of monocot leaf. In dicot leaf, the mesophyll cells are differentiated into palisade cells which are closely placed and spongy cells which are loosely placed. In dicot leaf, stomata are present on the lower surface. Thus sub-stomatal chambers are present only on the lower surface. In monocot leaf, stomata are present on the upper as well as the lower surface. Thus sub-stomatal chambers are present only on both the surfaces.

In marginal placentation, ovules are attached to the ridge formed on the ventral suture of the ovary. Pea plant has this arrangement. 97328.subject: Botany
97328.sol: Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity, e.g., heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur. In such plants, the leaves of the juvenile plant are different in shape from those in mature plants. On the other hand, difference in shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in buttercup also represent the heterophyllous development due to environment

97360.subject: Botany
97360.text: Essential requirement for seed germination is
97360.sol: Germination is the process of growth of a plant that eventually causes the formation of a seedling. Many factors like temperature, water, oxygen regulate the process of germination. Seed is very durable and can germinate in a wide range of temperatures. Essential requirements for the germination process are water and oxygen and germination cannot occur take in their absence. Seeds need oxygen for aerobic respiration to produce energy.

97530.subject: Botany
97530.text: Monocot plants are characterized by the presence of how many of the following characters? Scutellum, Reticulate venation, Fibrous roots, Stilt roots, Pulvinous leaf base, Isobilateral leaves
97530.sol: Monocot plants are group of Angiosperms that have a single cotyledon in their seed. These plants have a fibrous root system (adventitious) which develop from the plumule. The leaves have parallel venation with stomata on both surfaces and vascular bundles are both - small and large. The leaves are isobilateral as both surfaces appear similar. The cotyledon of monocots are generally referred to as scutellum as they are thin and shield shape.
